# Full-Stack Engineer (TypeScript / React) – Patient Experience

**Company:** Verdane Care (FICTIONAL)
**Location:** Graz, Austria (hybrid) or fully remote within Austria, Germany, Croatia or Slovenia
**Employment:** Full-time, permanent (or B2B contract in Croatia on request)
**Team:** Patient Experience squad (4 engineers, 1 designer, 1 product manager)

## About the role

Verdane Care makes appointment-booking and follow-up software for private clinics and physiotherapy practices. Patients use our web app and mobile web experience to book visits, fill in intake forms, receive reminders and view exercise plans.

As a Full-Stack Engineer you will build and improve those patient-facing features end to end – from React components and accessibility to the Node.js APIs and the database behind them. You will work in a small squad with a designer and a product manager, and you will ship to production several times a week.

## What you will do

- Build new patient-facing features in React and TypeScript, with a strong focus on accessibility (WCAG 2.2 AA) and performance on low-end phones
- Implement Node.js (NestJS) APIs and PostgreSQL schemas to support those features
- Integrate with third-party systems such as clinic calendars, SMS providers and payment gateways
- Write unit, integration and end-to-end tests (Jest, Playwright) and keep the build green
- Take part in design reviews, usability sessions and sprint planning
- Handle personal health data responsibly: follow our GDPR and data-minimisation guidelines, support audit requests from clinic customers
- Mentor interns or junior colleagues when the opportunity arises

## What you bring

**Must have**
- 2+ years of professional experience building web applications with React and TypeScript
- Experience writing backend services in Node.js (Express, NestJS or similar) and working with SQL databases
- Understanding of semantic HTML, responsive layouts and web accessibility basics
- Experience with automated testing (unit and end-to-end) and Git-based workflows
- Awareness of web security fundamentals (authentication, OWASP Top 10) and willingness to learn the privacy requirements of health data
- Fluent English; German or Croatian is helpful for customer-facing conversations

**Nice to have**
- Experience with Next.js or other server-side rendering frameworks
- Experience in healthcare, wellness or other regulated environments
- Familiarity with AWS or a similar cloud, and with Docker
- Experience with design systems and Storybook
- Experience with analytics and A/B testing

## What we offer

- Salary range EUR 54,000 – 70,000 gross per year depending on experience (Austrian collective agreement minimum applies)
- 25 days of holiday plus the Austrian public holidays, 5 additional well-being days and a EUR 1,200 yearly education budget
- Flexible hours, a home-office stipend and a yearly team retreat
- A friendly, low-ego team that cares about the people who use our software

## How to apply

Send your CV. A short cover letter and a link to something you have built (a portfolio, a GitHub project or a live site) are welcome but optional. We reply within ten working days.

Verdane Care is committed to a diverse and inclusive workplace and welcomes applications from career changers and people returning to work.

cover_letter_history.content:
Dear Verdane Care team,

I am a third-year Computing student and early-career web developer with hands-on experience building React and TypeScript interfaces, including a four-month software development internship and several academic and freelance projects. I am interested in the Full-Stack Engineer role because it brings together patient-facing features, accessibility, and practical full-stack development.

During my internship, I contributed accessibility fixes to a React news website and built a keyboard- and screen-reader-friendly image gallery for article pages, documenting the component in Storybook and testing it with Jest and React Testing Library. In my final-year project, Tidewatch, I built a React and TypeScript interface alongside a Node.js/Express API and PostgreSQL data storage. I tested the app with NVDA and VoiceOver and achieved a Lighthouse accessibility score of 100. I also built a wellness-oriented yoga studio booking site with Next.js, Tailwind CSS, static generation, and deployment on Vercel. In a separate React and JavaScript group project, I built login screens using Firebase Authentication. These projects have given me experience across frontend development, APIs, SQL data, and Jest and React Testing Library.

Verdane Care’s focus on patients, accessibility, and privacy by default particularly appeals to me. I would be keen to contribute my accessibility-minded development experience to software used by patients and care providers, while continuing to develop as a full-stack engineer. I have also supported approximately 30 students in first-year web development lab sessions, an experience that strengthened my ability to explain technical ideas and support others.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience and approach could contribute to the Patient Experience team.

Yours sincerely,
Aiyana Brooks-Tan

critique.content_quality_feedback: The cover letter is clear, professional, and appropriately concise. It presents the strongest relevant evidence in a logical order: the Harbourline Media internship, the Tidewatch project, the yoga studio site, and the Firebase Authentication project. The examples are specific and credible, particularly the keyboard- and screen-reader-friendly gallery, NVDA and VoiceOver testing, and Lighthouse score of 100. The closing is polite and targeted to the Patient Experience team. Its main limitation is that it does not address several important requirements, including the candidate's limited professional experience, Git-based workflows, end-to-end testing, semantic HTML, responsive layouts, and web security fundamentals. These are candidate-profile gaps rather than writing defects where the original material provides no supporting evidence.

Keyword coverage is good for the candidate's demonstrated experience. However, the letter does not contain evidence for Git, end-to-end testing, semantic HTML, responsive layouts, web security fundamentals, OWASP Top 10, or health-data privacy. Those terms should not be added because they are not supported by the candidate information. The wording is also somewhat dense in the second paragraph; shorter sentences would improve rapid recruiter and AI screening comprehension. AI screening probability is moderate-to-good for the demonstrated frontend, accessibility, testing, Node.js, SQL, and wellness-related experience, but limited for the full-stack role because the letter cannot substantiate the experience-level and security/testing requirements.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The letter aligns well with Verdane Care's accessibility, patient-focused, wellness-related, and practical full-stack themes. The Tidewatch project demonstrates React/TypeScript, Node.js/Express, PostgreSQL, automated testing, third-party API integration, and screen-reader testing. The yoga studio booking site supports the nice-to-have wellness and Next.js experience, while Storybook supports the design-system-related requirement. The candidate's experience is primarily a four-month internship, academic work, freelance work, and student projects, so the 2+ years of professional React/TypeScript experience requirement is a genuine gap. The material also does not establish end-to-end testing, Git-based workflows, semantic HTML, responsive layouts, web security fundamentals or OWASP knowledge, AWS/Docker, German/Croatian, or analytics/A/B testing. Fluent English is demonstrated by the letter itself. The statement about being interested in patient-facing software and privacy by default is relevant to the company's mission, but the candidate's direct experience is accessibility and wellness rather than healthcare or regulated health-data systems.
